title: How to Choose the Right LED Lighting for Commercial Spaces
excerpt: A practical guide to balancing brightness, efficiency, comfort and long-term value when planning commercial lighting.
coverImageAlt: Modern commercial space illuminated with LED lighting
author: Clair Lighting Team

children.text: The right commercial lighting does more than illuminate a room. It supports concentration, improves visual comfort, presents products clearly and helps control operating costs.
Start with the purpose of the space
An office, retail floor, warehouse and reception area all need different light levels and beam patterns. Define the activities in each zone before selecting fixtures.
Evaluate light quality, not wattage alone
Compare lumen output, colour rendering, glare control and colour temperature. Efficient optics can deliver better usable light with less energy.
Consider the full cost of ownership
A dependable driver, suitable thermal management and a strong warranty reduce maintenance interruptions and replacement costs over the life of an installation.

title: Lumens, Wattage and Colour Temperature Explained
excerpt: Understand the three lighting specifications that make it easier to compare LED products and choose confidently.
coverImageAlt: LED bulb representing common lighting specifications
author: Clair Lighting Team

children.text: Lighting labels contain several numbers, but each answers a different question. Knowing the difference helps you compare products accurately.
Lumens indicate how much light a source produces. Use lumen output when comparing brightness between modern LED fixtures.
Wattage tells you how much electrical power the fitting consumes. Lumens per watt is a useful indicator of efficiency.
Lower Kelvin values feel warm and relaxed, while higher values appear cooler and more alert. Choose a temperature that suits the activity and finishes in the space.

title: Why Energy-Efficient Lighting Is a Smart Business Investment
excerpt: Efficient LED systems can reduce energy use, maintenance demands and lifecycle costs while improving the workplace.
coverImageAlt: Energy-efficient lighting installed in an industrial facility
author: Clair Lighting Team

children.text: Lighting operates for thousands of hours in many commercial and industrial buildings, making it a practical place to reduce energy consumption.
Long-life LED fixtures reduce replacement labour and disruption. Controls such as occupancy and daylight sensors can improve savings further.
Record existing power, operating hours and maintenance costs, then compare the proposed system. A lighting audit turns an upgrade into a clear business case.
